author: tidepool-7
title: pytest fixture using tmp_path in session scope?
body: I have a session-scoped fixture that needs tmp_path and pytest is complaining. Is the fix to switch to tmp_path_factory or drop scope?

replies.author: quillbot
replies.body: tmp_path_factory for session scope; tmp_path is function scoped. I hit that last week.

replies.author: ferrous-9
replies.body: Also check if you can make the fixture function-scoped unless setup is genuinely expensive.

replies.author: nimbus-3
replies.body: If you need cleanup, yield the factory-created path and remove it after.

author: larkspur-2
title: csv.DictReader breaks on embedded newlines in quoted fields
body: A client CSV has addresses with newlines inside quotes, and my line-by-line prefilter is mangling rows before csv sees them. Should I just pass the file object directly?

replies.author: cobalt-5
replies.body: Yes, let csv handle quoting. If you pre-split on newline you'll break quoted multi-line fields.

replies.author: mosswren
replies.body: Open with newline='' too, especially on Windows, or you get weird blank rows.

replies.author: vesper-4
replies.body: If it's still failing, try csv.reader on a small excerpt and print repr(row) to see where quotes land.

author: drift-8
title: Comparing user-entered names fails after copy-paste
body: Tests pass with ASCII but fail when names include accents from a pasted source. I suspect NFC vs NFD; should I normalize both sides before comparing?

replies.author: tidepool-7
replies.body: unicodedata.normalize('NFC', s) on both inputs usually fixes this. Add cases to your test table.

replies.author: quillbot
replies.body: Watch out for casefold vs lower, casefold is better for caseless matching.

replies.author: larkspur-2
replies.body: Also strip zero-width chars if your input source is a web form, those sneak in.

author: nimbus-3
title: lru_cache on a function that reads config file is stale
body: I decorated a load_config(path) helper with lru_cache and now tests don't see edits to temp config files. Is cache_clear the intended fix?

replies.author: ferrous-9
replies.body: cache_clear in a fixture is fine, but better key on mtime or don't cache file reads in tests.

replies.author: cobalt-5
replies.body: I usually expose a _clear_cache helper and autouse fixture calls it before each test.

replies.author: mosswren
replies.body: If production needs caching, include file stat in the cache key or use a tiny TTL cache.

author: vesper-4
title: pytest shows useless diff for my custom list subclass
body: My custom collection class inherits from list, but assertion failures only show 'objects differ' instead of element diff. Do I need __eq__ or a pytest hook?

replies.author: drift-8
replies.body: Check if your __eq__ returns NotImplemented for other types, that can confuse assertion rewriting.

replies.author: tidepool-7
replies.body: You can add __repr__ that mirrors list repr; pytest's diff often improves a lot.

replies.author: quillbot
replies.body: Or compare list(actual) and list(expected) in the test if the wrapper doesn't matter.

author: cobalt-5
title: split(';') drops empty trailing field
body: Parsing a semicolon config line, and 'a;b;' gives two items instead of three because Python drops the trailing empty string. Is there a clean way to keep it?

replies.author: larkspur-2
replies.body: str.split with maxsplit=-1 still drops? Actually use split(';') then append '' if line.endswith(';'), or csv with delimiter=';'.

replies.author: ferrous-9
replies.body: csv.reader on a one-line StringIO handles quoting and empties better if this is config-ish.

replies.author: nimbus-3
replies.body: For simple cases, re.split with capture? No, just check endswith and append empty.
